signal: AirOps raised a $40M Series B led by Greylock at a $225M valuation, grew to nearly 100 employees, and launched a native Claude integration

email.body1:
Nick, saw AirOps close its $40M Series B with Greylock and ship the native Claude integration.

Scaling from 20 to nearly 100 people that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before the new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for AirOps off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nick, quick follow-up for AirOps.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late, and by then it's a scramble to recover the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings AirOps needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Nick, last bit of proof for AirOps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how AirOps' reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nick, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and the fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-B motion? I'll tailor it to AirOps either way.
